newsitem.title: USA: Iridium delays satellite launch one day.
newsitem.headline: Iridium delays satellite launch one day.

text.p: IRIDIUM LLC said Tuesday its planned launch of its first three satellites has been postponed a day until Thursday because of a "minor technical anomaly."
Motorola Inc has a 25 percent stake in IRIDIUM, a consortium that is working to provide a global telecommunications network using 66 low-orbit satellites.

IRIDIUM said the problem was detected in the ground system software which interprets the telemetry filed stored on board each satellite. It added that the error has been identified and the correction is now being "implemented and verified."
The new launch date has been moved to Thursday from Wednesday at Vandenberg Air Force Base in California.
IRIDIUM is an international consortium of 17 companies and organizations, including Motorola, Sprint Corp, Lockheed Martin Corp, Pacific Electric Wire & Cable Co, and Raytheon Co.
